title: Throughput & p95 SLA exploration - Helios Dynamics
header: Agenda: p95 targets, concurrency, streaming token/sec benchmarking, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
Attachments referenced: redwood-sizing.xlsx (shared), infra-diagram.png (link in chat), SOC2_summary.pdf
summary: Intro discovery call to map Helios' real-time inference SLOs. Primary goals: confirm p95 latency targets for streaming paths, expected concurrent sessions, token/sec burst profile, and evaluate hosted vs dedicated vs private given security needs.
topics: p95 latency targets for streaming and batch paths
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (cost, isolation, failover)
KV cache/prefix caching and its effect on p95
Quantization and model variants for throughput
Network egress, VPC options, KMS and audit logging
Suggested benchmarks and PoC next steps
transcript: 00:00 Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros?
00:07 Evan (Helios): Evan here, principal SWE on the realtime stack. We run low-latency routing for inference, mostly customer-facing chat and live summarization.
00:14 Priya (Helios): Priya, CTO. We're trying to lock down SLOs for Q4 rollout, big focus on p95 streaming latency.
00:20 Luis (Helios): Luis, SRE. I'll be driving the capacity planning and the runbook side.
00:27 Maya (Redwood SE): Maya from Redwood. I'll dig into the perf numbers and suggest test harnesses. Quick note — we shared a sizing sheet in the chat named redwood-sizing.xlsx.
01:05 Samir: Nice. Can you give us baseline numbers? What's your current p95 and concurrency?

01:12 Evan: Currently our p95 for streaming completions is around 320 ms end-to-end for short prompts (under 60 tokens) but that includes network and our proxy. Pure model-infer p95 we estimate ~220 ms. Concurrency — steady 120 concurrent streams, bursts up to 1.2k for 90s during events. Token/sec burst around 25k tokens/sec sustained for ~2 min then taper.
01:45 Priya: Our objective is p95 <= 250ms for streaming edges and p95 <= 300ms for heavier prompts. If we can't reach that on hosted, we want to explore Dedicated and Private.
02:02 Maya: Understood. Two quick clarifying questions — what's your average sequence length and how many tokens do you typically append per step?

02:10 Evan: Avg sequence length is 120 tokens, but most of the conversation windows are 40-80 tokens. Append per step is ~12 tokens. Also we have a lot of prefix reuse across similar sessions so prefix caching could help.

02:38 Maya: Good — prefix/KV cache will be big for you. On Redwood Hosted we do automatic KV caching and prefix caching for compatible models which can cut per-token latency significantly for repeat context. On Dedicated/Private you can tune cache sizes and colocate KV with the runtime.
03:00 Luis: For compliance we need SOC 2 type II, SSO (SAML), KMS integration, and audit logs that we can ship into our SIEM. Does Redwood hosted provide that?

03:10 Samir: Yes — hosted offers SAML, customer-managed KMS via cloud KMS options in dedicated tiers, and exportable audit logs. Private gives you the most control: full VPC, bring-your-own HSM. We'll attach SOC2_summary.pdf after the call.
03:34 Evan: Great. Cost is a factor. We want to understand the tradeoffs: if we push aggressive quantization, what's the p95 delta?

03:42 Maya: From our benchmarks, moving to 4-bit quantization on certain models reduces median and p95 for long sequences by ~20-35% but you can see a small quality delta depending on prompt types. For streaming small tokens the improvement is usually less dramatic but still meaningful. Also kernel selection and compilation paths affect tail latencies — we pick kernels per model/seq profile.
04:12 Priya: For bursts, is there an autoscale buffer? If we have 1.2k concurrent open streams spiking for 90s, what is your recommended architecture?

04:22 Samir: Two patterns. Hosted burst capacity: autoscaling with offer of burst credits but with some warm-up. Dedicated: reserved pool + configured burst nodes for predictable latency. Private: you control the pool and can pre-provision ephemeral capacity in your infra.
04:45 Luis: Warm-up feels risky. We need predictable p95 during spikes. Can we do canary warm-start or pre-warm kernels?

04:52 Maya: Yes — we have warm-start hooks and pre-warm policies. For Dedicated we can schedule model resident pools so that p95 stays stable during bursts. There's also a fallback policy to lighter variants if the heavy model can't meet SLOs.
05:20 Evan: How about streaming token throughput — tokens/sec per GPU? We run a mix of a 7B-ish model and a 13B variant. Any public numbers we can use to estimate headroom?

05:32 Maya: Rule of thumb: for optimized kernels, a single high-end A100 or equivalent can handle several thousand tokens/sec for 7B in streaming mode with batching; 13B is roughly 40-60% of that depending on sequence length and KV usage. We should run a lab benchmark with your real prompts to get exact tokens/sec. The sizing sheet we shared has placeholders where we can paste your prompt set; that will produce expected p95 and throughput curves.
06:12 Priya: We will provide prompt corpus. For p95 targets we care about end-to-end; how much network noise should we budget?

06:20 Samir: For hosted in a cloud region close to your clients, network added tail is usually 20-50ms. If you host in a different region or have complex proxy layers the network can add 100ms+. Private within your VPC will reduce network hops but you take on the infra reliability responsibility.
06:45 Luis: Any customers doing p95 200ms with streaming at 1k concurrency? Curious about real examples.

06:52 Maya: We have customers hitting p95 around 180-220ms for short tokens when using Dedicated with co-located routing and model-resident pools. They rely on aggressive caching + smaller quantized variants for latency-sensitive calls.
07:10 Evan: For the lab benchmark, can Redwood run an A/B of hosted vs dedicated with identical load profile?

07:18 Samir: Yes. Typical approach: 1) we'll ingest your prompt corpus and traffic profile, 2) spin up a benchmark harness that replicates token arrival patterns (burst shape, open streams), 3) run hosted baseline, then run on a Dedicated config we propose. We'll supply CSV of p50/p95/p99 and token/sec curves.
07:42 Priya: Do you require production data? We can't send PII. We can anonymize but we need assurances about retention.

07:50 Samir: We accept anonymized synthetic corpora. Redwood's hosted accepts opt-in retention and you can enable no-retention modes at the account level for the PoC. For Dedicated/Private, you control retention and logs.
08:12 Luis: What about replay and traceability? If an incident happens we need token-level traces for debugging but we also need them off by default for privacy.
08:20 Maya: We provide tracing hooks and per-request identifiers that can be turned on for debug windows. Audit logs are plumbed to your logging destination in Dedicated/Private.

09:00 Evan: A few architecture specifics — our proxy currently serializes requests through a central gateway which adds 60-80ms. We're considering moving to an edge aggregation to reduce that. How does Redwood assimilate into architectures with edge proxies?

09:13 Maya: Usually we recommend reducing proxy hops. You can place Redwood route points closer or use direct SDK calls from edge nodes. For Hosted, region placement matters; for Private you can colocate the runtime in your edge DC.
09:50 Priya: What's the timeline for the PoC? We want results in 3 weeks to decide for Q4 rollout.

09:58 Samir: 3 weeks is tight but feasible. Typical PoC timeline: week 1: dataset + sizing agreement; week 2: run benchmarks; week 3: analyze and iterate. We'll need a single point of contact — Luis for SRE and Evan for prompts.
10:20 Evan: Got it. For metrics, we will measure end-to-end p95, model-only p95, token/sec, and memory/GPU utilization. Anything else?
10:28 Maya: Also collect tail queue lengths, KV cache hit rates, and cold-start durations. Those explain p95 behavior more than medians.
11:05 Priya: What are typical fallback strategies? If heavy model can't meet p95 do you recommend a smaller model or returning partial results?

11:14 Maya: Two main fallbacks: 1) automatic routing to a lower-latency model variant (e.g., 7B quantized) and 2) partial streaming with summary tokens while continuing background completion. We can configure canary thresholds and A/B the quality impact.
11:40 Luis: On security — how does KMS integration work for Hosted? We need envelope encryption with our key provider.
11:48 Samir: Hosted supports customer-managed keys via cloud KMS in Dedicated tiers, and Private supports HSMs/BYOK. We'll detail the KMS flow in the SOC2 packet.
12:10 Evan: One detail on measuring p95: is the measurement anchored at the first token or last token emitted for streaming? We want consistency.

12:18 Maya: Good point. We report both start-to-first-token p95 and total completion p95. For streaming SLOs most people use first-token p95 or first-substantial-chunk p95 depending on UX expectations.
12:55 Priya: Any gotchas on sequence lengths changing mid-session and KV eviction? We've seen evictions spike latency.

13:03 Maya: Yes — eviction and KV cache churn cause tail spikes. Our runtime exposes eviction metrics and configurable cache sizes and TTLs. For your workload with heavy reuse it's beneficial to pin common prefixes.
13:28 Evan: Let's talk numbers — if we set a hard p95 target of 250ms for first-token streaming at 120 steady concurrency and 1.2k burst, what footprint do you estimate?

13:38 Maya: Ballpark: with optimized model variant and caching, Dedicated with 4-6 high-end GPUs (model-dependent) plus autoscale for bursts should meet p95 200-250ms. Hosted baseline might need additional regional placement and burst nodes — we'll show exact curves in the PoC. We'll put rough math in the sizing sheet.
14:05 Samir: We'll propose two configurations: conservative (predictable p95, Dedicated reserved + burst nodes) and cost-optimized (hosted with caching and lower-cost quantized variants).
14:25 Luis: For budgeting, what's the expected delta between hosted and dedicated per month for our profile?

14:31 Samir: We'll estimate in the pricing sheet. Expect Dedicated to be higher fixed but lower unit costs at sustained scale. Hosted is pay-as-you-go and can be cheaper initially but more variable for heavy sustained load.
15:02 Evan: For the benchmark harness — can you reproduce our exact burst shape (1.2k for 90s) and token distribution?

15:10 Maya: Yes — provide arrival rate histogram and sequence length distribution, and we'll replicate it. Also provide a small list of representative prompts and negative examples that stress hallucination/quality.
15:45 Priya: DevOps question — when we move to Dedicated, how much control do we get over kernel builds and container images?
15:53 Maya: Dedicated gives you image pinning, kernel flags control through our deployment config, and we can run private compiled kernels if requested for a managed services engagement.
16:20 Evan: Any unusual limits on streaming connections or token rates per connection?
16:28 Samir: There are soft limits which we can raise for PO C. The practical limit is per-instance throughput and connection management — during PoC we will instrument it.
16:55 Luis: Who do we loop in for legal and compliance for Private?
17:02 Samir: I'll intro you to our security team. We'll schedule a separate security review call to go over encryption, audit logs, and SLA terms.
17:18 Priya: Great. Can you also include an uptime SLA and p95 commitments in the proposal?
17:24 Samir: For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets in enterprise contracts; we'll include SLO language in the draft.
17:45 Evan: Anything about multi-region failover? We need to survive a region outage without p95 degradation beyond 2x for 10 mins.

17:53 Maya: Smart routing and cross-region fallbacks can route traffic to healthy regions with minimal retries. For strong p95 guarantees during failovers you'd want Dedicated across regions or Private multi-region deployment.
18:20 Luis: Ok let's recap next steps.

18:25 Samir: Recap — Redwood to run benchmarking PoC: hosted baseline + Dedicated config, using Helios prompt corpus and burst profile. Redwood to share detailed sizing + cost estimate. Security docs and SOC2 packet to be shared. Schedule security deep-dive next week.
18:45 Priya: Agreed. Timeline: dataset by Tuesday, run tests mid-next week, results by end of next week.
19:02 Evan: I'll anonymize prompts and send the arrival histograms. Luis will coordinate SRE access for any test endpoints.
19:22 Samir: Perfect. We'll attach the benchmark plan and test harness steps in email and link to the redwood-sizing.xlsx.
19:40 Maya: One more note — for p95 debugging we'll capture cold-starts and kernel-switch events; expect a short instrumentation stub we'll ask you to run.
19:55 Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
20:00 Samir: Thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the security call and the PoC kickoff. Bye.
